title: Smooth curves decompose into connected curves and rational points
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure] and let $C$ be a smooth separated finite-type $k$-scheme of dimension at most one (a smooth curve of [def-sc-curves]). There are a finite set $I$, smooth separated connected one-dimensional finite-type $k$-schemes $D_i$ for $i\in I$, and a finite set $J$, with an isomorphism of $k$-schemes $C\cong(\coprod_{i\in I}D_i)\amalg(\coprod_{j\in J}\operatorname{Spec}k)$. The coprojections are open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion] and closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion], and each index set may be empty. Coproducts are those of [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family].

source.place: Tag 0A5B, label lemma-constant-smooth-statements, first sentence of proof: finite disjoint union of smooth curves and points. Geometric justification: properties.tex Tags 0569 (lemma-regular-normal), 033N (lemma-normal-locally-Noetherian); varieties.tex Tag 06LH (lemma-algebraic-scheme-dim-0).

proof.text: Finite type over Spec k makes C locally Noetherian and quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Thus C is Noetherian. Use the existing connected-component quotient A = ConnectedComponents C. Noetherian spaces have open connected components; the quotient is discrete, and it is compact as the continuous image of C, hence A is finite. This uses the finite-component topology underlying [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finite-components], rather than reconstructing a finite intersection graph.

source.place: Tag 0BA8; topology.tex, finite-component argument for Noetherian spaces

proof.text: For a in A let V_a be the inverse image of {a} under C to ConnectedComponents C, as an open of C. It is closed because the quotient has closed singletons, nonempty and connected by the connected-component theorem, and these opens are pairwise disjoint and cover C. Its inclusion is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] and a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], using IsClosedImmersion.of_isPreimmersion and the closed range. Smoothness restricts by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes]. Composition of the closed immersion with the finite-type separated map f gives finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and separatedness [def-weil-proper-morphism] directly from the morphism-property instances.

source.place: Tag 0A5B, opening reduction; standard clopen open-subscheme construction

proof.text: Each V_a is locally Noetherian as an open subscheme. Smoothness gives regularity by [lem-sc-smooth-regular]; connectedness and nonemptiness give integrality by [lem-sc-regular-connected-integral]. By the inducing-map inequality for [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], its dimension is at most dim C, hence at most one by [def-sc-curves]. Integrality provides the nonempty irreducible closed set V_a itself, so its dimension is nonnegative. Case analysis on WithBot ENat shows that a value between zero and one is zero or one.

source.place: Tags 0569 and 033N; topology.tex, chains of irreducible closed subsets

proof.text: Partition the finite type A into the subtype I of dimension-one components and the complementary subtype J. The restrictions d_i on D_i = V_i are smooth connected curves by [def-sc-curves]. Each j in J has dimension zero by the dichotomy, so [lem-weil-pbc-zero-dim-integral-point] makes its actual structure morphism an isomorphism to Spec k. Use its inverse followed by V_j inclusion as the point inclusion. No arbitrary object is selected from an unproved existence theorem.

Form the family E on I + J of the D_i and Spec k and its maps alpha_s to C. Their open ranges are V_(r s), where r : I + J equiv A is Equiv.sumCompl. They are disjoint covering opens, so Mathlib nonempty_isColimit_cofanMk_of, the coproduct universal property [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], and Cofan.nonempty_isColimit_iff_isIso_sigmaDesc show that Sigma.desc alpha is an isomorphism. Let e be its inverse and q = Sigma.desc alpha followed by f. Sigma.ι_desc and the inverse identities prove all over-k equations. Coprojections are open immersions; since each composite with Sigma.desc alpha is the corresponding closed immersion alpha_s, IsClosedImmersion.of_comp gives their closed-immersion property. For empty C the connected-component quotient and both subtypes are empty, so the identical proof applies.

lean.statement: theorem smooth_curve_points_decomposition (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] (C : Scheme.{u}) (f : C ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsCurve f] [Smooth f] : ∃ (I J : Type u) (_ : Fintype I) (_ : Fintype J) (D : I → Scheme.{u}) (d : ∀ i, D i ⟶ Spec (.of k)), (∀ i, IsConnectedCurve (d i)) ∧ (∀ i, Smooth (d i)) ∧ ∃ (q : (∐ fun s : Sum I J ↦ match s with | Sum.inl i => D i | Sum.inr _ => Spec (.of k)) ⟶ Spec (.of k)), (∀ i, Sigma.ι (fun s : Sum I J ↦ match s with | Sum.inl i => D i | Sum.inr _ => Spec (.of k)) (Sum.inl i) ≫ q = d i) ∧ (∀ j, Sigma.ι (fun s : Sum I J ↦ match s with | Sum.inl i => D i | Sum.inr _ => Spec (.of k)) (Sum.inr j) ≫ q = 𝟙 _) ∧ ∃ (e : C ≅ ∐ fun s : Sum I J ↦ match s with | Sum.inl i => D i | Sum.inr _ => Spec (.of k)), e.hom ≫ q = f ∧ (∀ s, IsOpenImmersion (Sigma.ι (fun s : Sum I J ↦ match s with | Sum.inl i => D i | Sum.inr _ => Spec (.of k)) s)) ∧ (∀ s, IsClosedImmersion (Sigma.ι (fun s : Sum I J ↦ match s with | Sum.inl i => D i | Sum.inr _ => Spec (.of k)) s))
